slots.label: Evaporation
entries: Evaporation: the sun heats liquid water in the sea and in puddles, and the water turns into invisible water vapour that rises into the air.
slots.studentPrompt: Explain this step in your own words.

slots.label: Condensation
entries: Condensation: high up the air is cold, so the water vapour cools and turns back into tiny liquid drops, and billions of those drops gathered together form a cloud.
slots.studentPrompt: Explain this step in your own words.

slots.label: Precipitation
entries: Precipitation: the drops in the cloud join and grow bigger and heavier until gravity pulls them down to the ground as rain.
slots.studentPrompt: Explain this step in your own words.

slots.label: Collection
entries: Collection: the rain gathers in rivers, lakes and the sea, where the sun can heat it again - the cycle starts over and never ends.
slots.studentPrompt: Explain this step in your own words.

slots.label: Evaporation
entries: Liquid water turning into invisible water vapour when it is heated, for example by the sun.
slots.studentPrompt: Give your own example of this term.

slots.label: Water vapour
entries: Water in its gas form. It is invisible, but it is still water and it is still there in the air.
slots.studentPrompt: Give your own example of this term.

slots.label: Condensation
entries: Water vapour cooling down and turning back into tiny liquid water drops.
slots.studentPrompt: Give your own example of this term.

slots.label: Precipitation
entries: Water falling back to the ground, most often as rain, when drops grow too heavy to float.
slots.studentPrompt: Give your own example of this term.

slots.label: Collection
entries: Fallen water gathering together again in rivers, lakes and the sea.
slots.studentPrompt: Give your own example of this term.
